payment_plan.quote: For patients who qualify for charity and who are cooperating in good faith to resolve their discounted hospital bills, Little Colorado Medical Center may offer extended payment plans

notes: Policy covers emergency medical services in ER, services for conditions that would lead to adverse health changes if not promptly treated, non-elective services for life-threatening circumstances, and medically necessary services evaluated case-by-case.

Excluded providers: INNOVA-Emergency room providers, WIHCC-Winslow Indian Health Care Clinic Family practice physicians covering I.H.S. patients while working as inpatient hospitalists at LCMC. All other providers are covered.

Financial need determination includes individualized assessment, application process, use of external data sources, reasonable efforts to explore alternative payment sources, consideration of assets and financial resources, review of outstanding accounts and payment history.

Required documentation: completed Financial Assistance Application, copy of last year's tax return, last two months' income or bank statement for proof of income, checking and savings account balances, investment account balances.
Hospital must notify patient in writing within 30 days of receipt of completed application.
Re-evaluation of financial need at each subsequent service if last evaluation was more than 6 months prior or if additional relevant information becomes known.
Collection practices consider charity qualification, good faith effort to apply for governmental programs or charity, and good faith effort to comply with payment agreements.
For qualifying patients cooperating in good faith: extended payment plans may be offered, no outside collection agencies, cease all collection efforts.
No extraordinary collection actions (wage garnishments, liens on primary residences, other legal actions) without first making reasonable efforts to determine charity eligibility.

Reasonable efforts for collection: validate patient owes bills and all third-party sources identified/billed; documentation of offering charity application opportunity and patient non-compliance; documentation of offered payment plan not honored.
If collection agency identifies patient meeting financial assistance criteria, account may be considered for financial assistance, collection suspended, application reviewed.
If entire account balance adjusted, account returned. If partial adjustment, patient fails to cooperate, or patient not eligible, collection activity resumes.
Management must comply with all federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations.
Amounts charged for emergency and medically necessary services will not exceed amounts generally billed to individuals with insurance covering such care.
Look-back method used for calculating amounts generally billed based on actual past claims paid by Medicare fee-for-service only or Medicare fee-for-service together with all private health insurers.
Itemized statement provided to patient showing charges and discount amount applied.
Discount applied once patient submits complete application for financial assistance.
Hospital may use outside agencies to estimate income for charity eligibility determination when no evidence supports eligibility.
Policy does not consider race, creed, gender, national origin, disability, age, social immigrant status, or sexual orientation in granting financial assistance.
